summary: Much better: the scull is now symmetric (hands at x +2.78/-2.78 on F000, sweeping in to about +/-1.8 on F015), the elbows open and close with drag, the knees circle and the bob is visible. No pops, seam closed, no intersections. What remains is mechanical regularity: the two arms are exact mirror images on every frame, most of the body still changes direction on frames 15 and 45, and the feet are still frozen.

findings.observation: metrics: twinning on UpperArm.ry, UpperArm.rz and LowerArm.rx (left and right are mirror-identical on every frame), lockstep with 8 of 13 bones keyed on frames 15 and 45, overlap_score 0.628 (below the 0.75 bar). On the sheets the two arms reach their widest (F000, F030) and closest (F015-F018, F045-F048) on exactly the same frames, which reads as a machine rather than someone treading water. Mirrored sculling is correct, so the shape is kept; only the timing is loosened: the whole right arm is delayed 2 frames and both shins 2 frames behind the thighs. Dry-run on iteration 1: no twinned channels, no frame with 7 or more bones keyed, no pops, no intersections; hands stay within 0.1 stud of symmetric (x +2.78/-2.70 on F000).

Foot.rx is a flat 20 on both feet for all 60 frames (curves.png), so the kick ends in rigid paddles. The feet now point (34) about 3 frames after each knee extends and relax (16) as it bends, opposite on the two sides.
